newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius posts 6.0 pct inflation in July.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius posts 6.0 pct inflation in July.

text.p: The central Bank of Mauritius said July year-on-year inflation was 6.0 percent.

The figure, published in its August report on Friday, represented a 0.2-percent increase over the 5.8 percent annual inflation rate that the Mauritius economic planning ministry posted for the financial year ended 30 June 1996.
No inflation forecast is yet available for the 1996/97 year, and the bank did not give a year-on-year figure for June alone.
The bank said the overall weighted yield from treasury bills' weekly auctions and the bank rate increased in August.

"The overall weighted yield for the month of August stood at 9.31 percent, up from 9.13 percent in the previous month, while (the) overall bank rate was at 9.54 percent, 18 basis points higher than the figure of 9.36 percent for July 1996," it said.
The "Bank rate fluctuated between 9.51 percent and 9.61 percent versus the previous month range of 9.31-9.48 percent, reflecting a general upward trend in the month of August 1996," it said.
The report said the central bank auctioned a total 2.625 billion rupees ($127.6 million) of treasury bills in August.

"In July 1996, a marked preference was noted for the 91-day bills. During August, however, bidders opted predominantly for the 182-day bills, which accounted for around 44 percent of total bids received," the report said.
In July, the bank put 3.125 billion rupees of treasury bills on auction, received 3.231 billion rupees of bids and sold 2.848 billion rupees worth of bills.
In the foreign exchange market, the report said the central bank sold a total $38 million to commercial banks during interventions in August, up from $29 million in July.

Central bank purchases from the interbank forex market was nil in July and August. In August, intervention rates ranged between 20.1492 and 20.4487 per dollar while the daily average interbank ask rate was between 20.1207 and 20.3065.
The report said the Mauritius Sugar Syndicate sold an equivalent total of $9.65 million directly to banks in August.
As from the 1996 harvest season, the Syndicate is putting on tender sale to the banking sector 25 percent of the country's sugar export hard currency receipts, which are predominantly in pounds.
The Syndicate held its first tender sale on August 13 and is expected to sell a total equivalent amount of 2 billion rupees for the year 1996/97.
The central bank report said the rupee fell by 0.73 percent against the dollar and 0.53 percent against the pound from July 1996 to August 1996.
The rupee slipped 0.89 percent on the dollar and 1.59 percent on the pound from June to July 1996.
Between August 1995 and August 1996, the rupee weakened 10.85 percent against the dollar and 9.76 percent on the pound.
"The foreign exchange reserves of the Bank of Mauritius fell marginally by 1.1 percent from 14,787 million rupees in July to 14,625 million rupees at the end of August 1996," it said.

It added these reserves represented 21.1 weeks of imports on the value of import bill for the fiscal year 1995-96. At July end, foreign exchange reserves of the central bank represented 21.4 weeks of imports.
($1=20.567 Mauritian rupees).
